1.
Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned brief holder for the State apprised the Court that on 20.02.2023 notice has been served to the informant of the case.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

2. Heard Ms. Sweta Nishad Advocate holding brief of Sri Akash Kumar Nishad, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned brief holder for the State-respondent.
3.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
488 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and 5(J)(2)/6 POCSO Act, Police Station- Kotwali Deoria, District- Deoria, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members on 18.07.2022 and according to the FIR, on 18.06.2022 applicant and his family members enticed away the daughter of Rohit Maddheshiya vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: 1 the informant aged about 17 years and informant received an information that they have taken her to Kolkata and wanted to sell her.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and FIR of the present case was lodged after more than a month from the date of alleged enticement and this fact clearly suggests that it is based on false and frivolous facts.

6. She further submitted that although, there is allegation of selling of the victim against applicant and his family members but when the statements of the victim were recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. then she did not make any allegation against the applicant and categorically stated that she had gone along with the applicant according to her own wish but under the pressure of her parents she stated that applicant duped her although, from her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it appears that with her consent physical relationship was developed between applicant and victim.

She further submitted that as per the ossification test report of the victim, she was more than 20 years' old and even according to her school record, she was more than seventeen and half years' old.
7.
She further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 10.08.2022 i.e. for more than a year.

8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that from the record, it reflects that by playing fraud applicant had taken the victim and thereafter against her wishes made physical relationship with her but could not dispute the fact that as per the ossification test report,
victim was more than 20 years' old at the time of incident and even as per her school record, she was more than seventeen and half years' old and applicant is in jail for more than a year.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. From the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C., it appears that she had gone along with the applicant according to her own wish and she permitted the applicant to make physical relationship with her.
11. Further, even from the school record of the victim, she appears to be more than 17 years of age and according to the CMO report, her radiological age was more than 20 years.
12. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since August, 2022 i.e. for more than a year.
13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

sentences.text:
15. Let the applicant- Rohit Maddheshiya be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 19.9.2023 KK Patel  Rohit Maddheshiya vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180387484/
